title: Economic Parity in the Post-Digital Age
author: Cornelia Team
excerpt: A comprehensive analysis of workforce shifts and the evolving barriers to female financial autonomy in emerging markets. This report explores systemic shifts required for true equity.
content: Project Cornelia is a women-led organisation that strives for active participation of every woman in the modern democratic discourses of this country.

Our journey from a student-run club to now an independent organisation (legally known as the AINA Foundation) is reflective of our determination and commitment to fight the various gender-based inequalities prevalent in the society. In the past 3.5 years, we have conducted more than 30 awareness activities to educate and empower more than 300 females on issues ranging from domestic violence, street and gender harassment to the rights of acid attack survivors.
As a one-of-a-kind organisation in India, we envision helping women at grassroot levels voice their opinions and exercise their choices, as they become informed and fearless.

title: The Matriarchal Legacy of the Deccan
author: Cornelia Team
excerpt: Tracing historical matrilineal structures through rediscovered oral traditions.
content: Throughout history, matrilineal societies have shaped the course of civilizations.
The Deccan region holds rich oral traditions about women's leadership and property rights.
Our research uncovers these forgotten narratives and their relevance to contemporary feminist thought.

title: Digital Literacy as Human Right
author: Cornelia Team
excerpt: Why bridging the gendered tech divide is the most critical intervention for the next decade.
content: Digital access remains a critical barrier for women in emerging economies.
Technology education and literacy programs must be gender-sensitive and trauma-informed.
This paper outlines policy recommendations for bridging the digital divide.

title: Redefining the Narrative: New Archives Discovered in Goa
author: Cornelia Team
excerpt: Researchers have unearthed a significant collection of letters and manuscripts dating back to the 18th century, offering unprecedented insights into the social standing and property rights of women in coastal communities during the transition to colonial rule.
content: The discovery of historical archives provides new perspectives on women's agency.
Colonial records often obscured women's roles in society.
These newly discovered documents challenge traditional historical narratives.

title: Policy Brief: Addressing the Invisible Care Economy
author: Cornelia Team
excerpt: Our latest data-driven brief quantifies the unpaid labor market and provides a framework for integrating care-work recognition into national GDP calculations, a move supported by major economic activists.
content: Care work, predominantly performed by women, is systematically undervalued.
Economic models must account for unpaid domestic and care labor.
Policy interventions can recognize and redistribute care responsibilities equitably.

title: Annual Symposium: Reclaiming Historical Voices
author: Cornelia Team
excerpt: A recap of our flagship event where scholars from twelve countries gathered to discuss the methodology of reading against the grain in official archives to find the silenced narratives of women.
content: Our annual symposium brings together scholars, activists, and community members.
The focus this year was on methodologies for uncovering women's histories.
Presentations highlighted marginalized voices in archival research.

title: The Power of Women in Policy Making
author: Cornelia Team
excerpt: Exploring how women's participation in policy discussions can lead to more inclusive and effective governance.
content: When women participate in policy decisions, outcomes improve.
Gender diversity in governance leads to more comprehensive solutions.
Barriers to women's political participation must be systematically dismantled.

title: Amplifying Marginalized Voices
author: Cornelia Team
excerpt: A deep dive into our initiatives aimed at bringing marginalized communities into the center of democratic conversations.
content: Marginalized communities must be at the table when decisions are made.
Cornelia works to amplify voices often silenced in mainstream discourse.
Grassroots organizing is essential for democratic participation.

title: Student Leadership in Social Change
author: Guest Author
excerpt: How student-led initiatives like Cornelia are driving meaningful social and policy change in their communities.
content: Young people are leading transformative movements worldwide.
Student organizations can bridge the gap between activism and policy.
The future depends on empowering young leaders with tools and platforms.

title: Building Community Through Dialogue
author: Cornelia Team
excerpt: The importance of creating safe spaces for conversations and how it strengthens community bonds.
content: Safe spaces for dialogue are foundational to community building.
Conversation circles have transformed how women share experiences.
Trust and confidentiality are essential for authentic connection.

title: Supporting Acid Attack Survivors
author: Cornelia Team
excerpt: Our fundraising initiatives and the broader work being done to support and empower acid attack survivors.
content: Acid attack survivors face immense physical and psychological trauma.
Cornelia's support programs focus on rehabilitation and livelihood.
Legal justice and social acceptance are crucial components of healing.

title: Democracy Needs Women's Voices
author: Guest Author
excerpt: Why gender equality in democratic participation is essential for building a stronger, more equitable society.
content: Democracy without women's equal participation is incomplete.
Gender diversity strengthens democratic institutions and processes.
Building equitable democracies requires deliberate policy interventions.
